newsitem.title: USA: Hughes, PanAmSat to merge satellite services.
newsitem.headline: Hughes, PanAmSat to merge satellite services.

text.p: Hughes Electronics Corp. agreed to buy satellite operator PanAmSat Corp. for $3 billion in cash and stock that will merge the two companies' satellite services operations, Hughes announced Friday.
Under the agreement, Hughes Electronics' Hughes Communications Galaxy (HCG) business will merge with Greenwich, Conn.-based PanAmSat to create a new company called PanAmSat Corp., the companies said.
Hughes, a General Motors Corp. unit which has been aggressively moving into high-growth data and communications services, will become a global leader in satellite services, Wall Street analysts said.
"It's an excellent idea for Hughes," said analyst Cai Von Rumohr of Cowen & Co.
The new company will combine HCG's fleet of 10 communications satellites for the U.S. market with PanAmSat's international fleet of four communications satellites.
PanAmSat has four satellites under construction and HCG has three in development. All are planned for launch through 1998. PanAmSat and HCG had combined 1995 revenues of about $500 million.

Under terms of the agreement, PanAmSat shareholders will get a total $1.5 billion in cash and 28.5 percent of the new company. Hughes Electronics will own 71.5 percent of the new company immediately after the merger.

Mexican media giant Televisa, which had been trying to sell its 40.5 percent stake in PanAmSat, said Friday it expects to receive about $600 million in cash and an equity interest of about 8.5 percent as result of the deal.
Analysts said the deal gives GM another reason to sell Hughes, which has changed direction since the automaker acquired it in 1985 for more than $5 billion.
Hughes has been going into "businesses that just are not a part of GM," said John Modzelewski, an analyst at PaineWebber Group Inc.

For months Wall Street has speculated GM may want to spin off Hughes. Hughes Chairman C. Michael Armstrong has hinted he would prefer his company operate independently. At a news conference in New York Friday, he declined to speculate on a possible spinoff.

HCG is a leading provider of commercial video, voice and data satellite communications services in the United States. Its Galaxy fleet serves premier cable and broadcast television programmers, with access provided by HCG's Galaxy Network Operations unit in Long Beach, Calif.

"By combining Hughes' and PanAmSat's strengths in domestic and global satellite communications, we will be bringing a new level of service to our customers throughout the world," said Armstrong. "Satellites have proven to be one of the most effective and competitive ways to communicate, whether by voice, computer, fax or video, by anyone, from anyplace, at anytime to anywhere on the planet."

Hughes has been diversifying in recent years away from its traditional staple as a maker of satellites and missiles into high-growth consumer services such as DirecTV, its consumer satelite television operation.

"It's clear to everybody that the value of Hughes is becoming less and less what it was just a year or two ago," analyst Modzelewski said. "This was a defence company that was going to link up with (auto electronics unit) Delco and we were going to have aerospace technology make its way into GM cars."
Under the deal, PanAmSat shareholders will have three options for payment with respect to the about 100 million outstanding shares of PanAmSat common stock.
The companies said they will be able to choose between $30 in cash, one share of new PanAmSat common stock, or half a share of new PanAmSat common stock and $15 in cash.
The new PanAmSat Corp.'s corporate headquarters will be in Greenwich, Conn., with domestic operations based in Long Beach and international operations based in Greenwich.

The deal requires government review and approval of the Federal Communications Commission, which are expected to be completed within six to 12 months. Although it is subject to PanAmSat shareholder approval, PanAmSat shareholders owning in excess of 90 percent of the voting power have agreed to vote in favour of the transaction, the companies said.
PanAmSat stock fell 12.5 cents to $27.625 Friday on Nasdaq, and GM Hughes, which trades separately from the automaker's stock, slipped $2.50 to $60.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
